transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Iris Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Ridgeview Head of ML), Tom Bennett (Ridgeview VP Eng), Lena Ortiz (Ridgeview Security), Jonah Park (Ridgeview Infra)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Maya AE on the account, Carlos is our SE, Iris is the CSM. Ridgeview, want to hear where you are and what success looks like.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, thanks. we run an insights product for retail clients, lots of long contexts in prompts, average request is around 1500-2k tokens. main concern is unit cost, we have a hard budget per monthly active user. Also latency matters but within a 300-500ms per response window is okay for batched ops.
[00:35] Tom: Yeah, from eng side we need predictability. spikes happen end of day and during promo windows. We're trying to decide whether to start hosted for time-to-value or go straight to Dedicated. Private is interesting for some enterprise customers with residency.
[00:52] Carlos: Got it. quick question on existing stack? where do you currently host models, any in-house infra?
[00:58] Jonah: We have an internal TF serving + smaller LLM proxies for embeddings. But ops overhead is high. Not enough throughput for our expected query rates without big infra spend.
[01:15] Maya: Ok. high level — Redwood hosted gives you fastest onboarding; per-token pricing with tiers. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for predictability and lower per-token unit cost when you hit commit levels. Private is our VPC/on-prem route for residency and full control. Main levers for cost are batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization choices.
[01:41] Priya: Can you give concrete numbers or examples? It's hard to judge without a model of our 2k-token prompts.
[01:47] Carlos: Sure. rough example, for a 2k-token response — if you do single-request lower batching and no cache, hosted per-token can be higher, say X cents/token (note: placeholder on call, we'll send exact bands). If you enable prefix/KV cache and a batch size of 16 with continuous batching, you can cut per-token CPU/GPU time dramatically — that maps to a drop in unit cost.
[02:14] Tom: When you say KV cache, is that only for repeated prefixes or does it work across users? how stateful is it?
[02:20] Carlos: It depends on policy. we do prefix caching per-model-per-customer; you can configure cache windows and privacy. For shared prompts across users, you see big gains; for one-off prompts less so. Also, caching interacts with latency SLAs — if we hit a cache warmup, first request may be slower.
[02:40] Lena: security question — for Dedicated and Private, how do you handle KMS and key residency? we have to ensure keys are customer-controlled, HSM backed ideally. SOC 2 is a must.
[02:50] Maya: totally — we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated can integrate with an enterprise KMS in a VPC. SOC 2 reports are available; we'll send the security pack.
[03:02] Priya: our cost target is approximately $0.12 per active user per month for inference on a minimum viable feature. rough math: 200k monthly queries, avg 2k tokens => budget constrained.
[03:16] Carlos: ok that's actionable. two paths: start hosted to get rolling and instrument token-level metrics; then move to Dedicated when you can commit to a monthly GPU pool which reduces per-token price. or run a Private pilot if data residency is non-negotiable.
[03:33] Tom: What about burst capacity? we have spikes. can Dedicated burst into hosted or other zones?
[03:39] Maya: Yes, we have routing policies — Dedicated can be primary and fallback to hosted (or cheaper model variants) for overflow. There's also auto-burst options we can configure. Fallback model variants may be quantized smaller models to preserve SLA during overload.
[03:58] Jonah: curious about quantization. does Redwood handle quantized models or do we ship quantized weights?
[04:03] Carlos: Our runtime supports INT8/4 quantized paths and selects kernels based on model. We can onboard quantized variants; sometimes we recommend a quantized fallback for low-latency, low-cost paths. We'll include guidance per model.
[04:21] Priya: ok for success metrics on pilot — we want a target of median latency <400ms for 95th percentile under normal traffic, and per-token unit cost within 20% of your modeled dedicated price. Also quality regression must be tracked vs baseline.
[04:37] Iris: good to capture. we'll propose an eval set and quality checks.
[04:42] Maya: Perfect. quick clarification on billing: hosted is usage-based per token. Dedicated is commit+usage; private is licensing + infra. In Dedicated you get lower unit rates after commit thresholds. We'll send an example cost spreadsheet mapping throughput to effective per-token price.
[05:03] Tom: Any examples of customers who've migrated from hosted to dedicated and what delta in unit cost they saw? numbers help our CFO.
[05:11] Carlos: Yes — anonymized: one customer cut effective per-token costs by ~40% after moving to Dedicated with 3-month commit, mostly because batching increased and KV cache hit rates improved. We'll send a case study.
[05:25] Priya: about batching — how does queuing affect latency? our UX team worries about stalls.
[05:31] Carlos: there's a tradeoff. continuous batching groups small requests to improve throughput but adds queuing latency. For interactive features we tune to lower batch sizes (4-8). For async or offline jobs we can use batch sizes 32-64 to maximize efficiency. We can set per-route SLOs in the Console.
[05:52] Jonah: do we need to change prompts to get better caching?
[05:55] Carlos: yes, prompt engineering helps. canonicalizing prefixes and extracting shared instruction tokens increases cache hit rates. We'll share examples.
[06:05] Speaker 3: Mm-hmm.
[06:07] Maya: A bit about pilot scope — recommended initial pilot: 2 weeks of synthetic load + 2 weeks of real traffic shadowing, include a sample of your 2k-token prompts, measure latency, cache hits, and cost. We'll instrument per-route token breakdown and token-level cost.
[06:22] Priya: timing — we want to ship an MVP by end of Q1; pilot needs to start mid-December ideally.
[06:29] Maya: ok. we'll aim for pilot kickoff week of Dec 8.
[06:33] Lena: about encryption in transit and at rest — for Hosted, are customer payloads encrypted with customer keys?
[06:39] Maya: hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default, but we offer envelope encryption options and tokenization patterns; for strict KMS control Private/Dedicated are better. We'll detail options.
[06:52] Tom: curious on observability — can we get token-level cost and tracing per request?
[06:57] Iris: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-model routing traces, latency histograms, and retention windows. We can configure logs to forward to your Splunk/Datadog.
[07:10] Priya: if we do a pilot, what are success criteria? let's be explicit: 1) average cost per 1k tokens below X (placeholder) 2) 95p latency < 500ms for interactive subset 3) quality degradation < 2% vs baseline.
[07:25] Carlos: that's reasonable. we'll collaborate on the evaluation harness.
[07:31] Maya: quick objection we usually see from finance: why not in-house?
[07:36] Tom: we asked that — in-house is cheaper at scale but ops + experimentation tax is high. we need to evaluate total cost of ownership.
[07:44] Maya: Exactly — Redwood aims to reduce ops burden and provide predictable unit economics. Our Optimize toolkit recommends batching and quantization settings to hit cost targets.
[07:55] Priya: On competitors — some teams prefer Anthropic/OpenAI. are there feature differences to highlight?
[08:02] Carlos: Main differences are in model catalog, data residency, and routing flex. We'll send a competitor note. For us, the differentiator is the unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private and explicit levers for cost.
[08:18] [10:12] Tom: small interruption — connectivity issues; back now.
[10:22] Lena: Can you include a security appendix with SOC2, penetration test cadence, and your retention policy?
[10:27] Maya: yes, will include in the security pack.
[10:31] Priya: about pricing bands — if we commit to a 12-month Dedicated contract, what's the rough discount vs hosted?
[10:37] Maya: depends on commit and model; typical commitments yield 30–50% effective reduction in unit cost given higher batching and reserved capacity. We'll send a modeled spreadsheet with your traffic to show break-even point.
[10:52] Carlos: For the benchmark we'll ask for a sample prompt set and a smaller sample dataset for privacy. we can run with synthetic tokens to emulate your 2k avg length.
[11:03] Jonah: do you support hybrid routing per tenant? i.e., some customers on Private, some on Hosted?
[11:08] Carlos: yes. multi-tenant routing decisions are configurable; you can route by customer id, route, or token budget.
[11:18] Priya: any gotchas on cold starts with Dedicated?
[11:21] Carlos: Dedicated avoids many cold start issues since capacity is reserved. cold starts are more an issue with serverless-like scaling; but model swapping and large context windows can add overhead.
[11:34] Maya: wrap-up: action items and next steps — we'll send pricing spreadsheet and security pack, Carlos runs bench and shares results, Iris will send onboarding checklist, and we schedule pilot kickoff for week of Dec 8.
[11:52] Tom: Sounds good. thanks all.
[12:00] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with the doc bundle.

End of transcript.
